description: Daily nutrient targets for one person from the EFSA rows served by GET /reference-intakes. Select rows: population Adults (age >= 18) or Children, age band ageFrom <= age <= ageTo in years, sex from the basis (pregnancy and lactation force female; "average" computes female and male completely, then averages each field). Variants: energy keeps the row whose pal equals the profile PAL; zinc keeps "(LPI n mg/day)" with n = phytateMgPerDay (600 when absent); "Postmenopausal" rows are kept only when the profile is postmenopausal AND such a row matches the age, otherwise they are dropped. Rows with no number (ND, NA.) and rows whose nutrientKey is null are ignored. Fields: ar_kcal -> energy point target (min = max); pri, else ai -> min; ri -> min/max range; ul -> upperLimit; ar in other units and ssi are not targets. Pregnancy and lactation rows (matched on "Nth trimester" or "0–6"/">6 months post partum" when the description names a period) are added to the base value when isIncrement, else replace it. Units: g/kg bw per day x weightKg; E% x energy target / (100 x kcal per g: carbohydrates 4, protein 4, fat 9, saturated fat 9), after any energy increment; g/mg/µg per day converted to the key's unit (suffix Kcal, G, Mg, Ug); U+03BC and U+00B5 are the same micro sign. Rounding half-up: kcal and g to whole numbers, mg and µg to one decimal. Output sorted by nutrientKey; sources are the links of the rows used, sorted and de-duplicated (a replaced base row is not cited). Under 1 year, and pregnancy or lactation under 18, are unsupported.

cases.why: Man, 30, PAL 1.6, 75 kg. Energy 2588 kcal; protein 0.83 x 75 = 62.25 -> 62 g; carbs 45-60 % of 2588 / 4 = 291.15-388.2 -> 291-388 g; fat 20-35 % / 9 = 57.5-100.6 -> 58-101 g; calcium uses the >= 25 band (950); zinc defaults to LPI 600 (11.7); sodium SSI and the vitamin D UL in VDE are not targets.

Woman, 30, PAL 1.4, 60 kg. Energy 1813; protein 0.83 x 60 = 49.8 -> 50; carbs 1813 x 45-60 % / 4 = 203.96-271.95 -> 204-272; fat 1813 x 20-35 % / 9 = 40.3-70.5 -> 40-71; iron uses the premenopausal 16 mg; zinc LPI 600 female 9.3.
A postmenopausal woman of 52 gets EFSA's postmenopausal iron PRI of 11 mg, not the premenopausal 16 mg.
EFSA has no postmenopausal iron value under 40, so a postmenopausal woman of 35 keeps the 16 mg value rather than getting no iron target at all.
The "average" basis is for people who give no sex: energy (2588 + 2072) / 2 = 2330, iron (11 + 16) / 2 = 13.5, zinc (11.7 + 9.3) / 2 = 10.5 with the shared UL 25.

Woman, 28, PAL 1.6, 65 kg, 2nd trimester: energy 2147 + 260 = 2407; protein 0.83 x 65 + 9 = 62.95 -> 63; iron replaced by the pregnancy value 16 (only its source cited); zinc 9.3 + 1.6 = 10.9; carbs from the pregnancy RI on the raised energy, 2407 x 45-60 % / 4 = 270.8-361.05 -> 271-361. The basis says male on purpose: pregnancy always computes with the female values.
Lactation increments are additive and the protein one depends on the post-partum period: woman, 30, 60 kg, 0-6 months: energy 2072 + 500 = 2572; protein 49.8 + 19 = 68.8 -> 69.
After six months post partum the protein increment drops to 13 g: 49.8 + 13 = 62.8 -> 63, while the energy increment stays 500.
Zinc absorption falls with dietary phytate: a man on a high-phytate diet (LPI 1200) gets 16.3 mg instead of the default 11.7.
Age bands are inclusive at both ends: at 24 the 18-24 band applies, 1000 mg.
One year later the >= 25 band takes over, 950 mg: the age on the day decides, so the target moves on a birthday.
The activity level picks the energy row: a very active man of 25 (PAL 2.0) gets 3340 kcal, not the 2672 of PAL 1.6.
Under 18 the Children rows apply: boy of 15, PAL 1.6, 60 kg: energy 2699, protein 0.88 x 60 = 52.8 -> 53, iron 11, calcium 1150.
Sodium SSI, an energy AR in MJ and a vitamin D UL in VDE (no nutrientKey) are not targets: only the vitamin D AI remains, written with the Greek mu.
EFSA pregnancy rows start at 18; a pregnant 16-year-old gets "unsupported" so the app sends her to a professional instead of guessing.
Under one year old the journal makes no target at all: infant feeding is out of scope.
